title: Compose the approval policy contract into the daemon approval path
description:
CONSUMER EDGE for task-5d8f11c86a3a41b4a8a420ef0d52a444, which landed the contract as a PURE @moe/core module with NO consumer. Clause 1 requires this task to exist; it is the primary consumer.

WHAT LANDED AND IS READY TO COMPOSE (commit 18f0964, verify before planning — task rail 6 says a description's claims about disk are stale by default):
- packages/core/src/planning/approval-policy.ts — APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS (frozen, ["PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN","REQUIRE_HUMAN"]), the ApprovalPolicy union with a REQUIRED delayMs on the auto arm, and decideApprovalAuthority(request) -> ApprovalAuthorityResult.
- packages/core/src/planning/approval-authority.ts — HumanAuthorityGate, HumanAuthorityGrant, grantHumanAuthority, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES (8), APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS (2).
- All five values are published from the @moe/core ROOT (index-surface.test.ts pins 80).
- checkHumanAuthority and refuseApprovalAuthority are deliberately NOT published: decideApprovalAuthority is the only intended entry point, because it consults the gate FIRST by construction. Do not reach around it.

THE GAP THIS TASK CLOSES: nothing imports the contract. The daemon can still approve a plan with no policy consulted and no gate checked, which is the state the contract was written to end.

SCOPE: compose decideApprovalAuthority in front of the existing plan.approve path in apps/daemon, and persist the HumanAuthorityGate on the unit of work. approvePlan (packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-submission.ts:172) and its reducer arm (planning-run-reducer.ts:174) must keep their current behaviour for UNGATED work with their existing tests green and UNMODIFIED — the policy composes IN FRONT of them, it does not replace them.

CRITICAL, from the incident that motivated the contract: the gate must be persisted on the WORK'S OWN DURABLE IDENTITY, not as a lifecycle/status field. On 2026-08-15 a bulk promotion of every BLOCKED task cleared each task's recorded blockedReason; a gate stored like a status would have been cleared the same way. approval-authority.ts's module comment states this and is worth reading before designing the persistence.

FOR THE CONSUMER, a hazard the contract documents but cannot enforce: ApprovalAuthorityDecision.delayMs is a safe non-negative integer, which is WIDER than setTimeout accepts. A delay above 2**31-1 CLAMPS TO 1ms, so "effectively never" silently becomes "immediately". Bound it here, where the timer lives.

NOT IN SCOPE: the control-room surface (its own task), the orchestrator settings file (its own task), changing the contract itself.
definitionOfDone: The daemon's plan-approval path calls decideApprovalAuthority and honours its verdict; a gated unit of work cannot be approved through the daemon under any approval policy, proved by a test that drives the real daemon handler rather than the core function.
The HumanAuthorityGate is persisted on the unit of work's durable identity, and a test proves a bulk status transition does NOT clear it - the exact mechanism of the 2026-08-15 incident.
Every daemon-level refusal asserts the stable code AND the refusing layer from APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES / APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS, never merely that approval did not happen.
approvePlan and its plan.approve reducer arm keep their current behaviour for ungated work, with their existing tests green and unmodified.
delayMs is bounded before it reaches any timer, with a test pinning the behaviour above 2**31-1 rather than letting it clamp to 1ms.
A mutation drill removing the decideApprovalAuthority call turns a named daemon test red on its refusal assertion, restored byte-exact and verified by hash.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE, AND CORRECT THE COMMAND NAME BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. No production bytes written.

1. THE NAME. The description says "the existing plan.approve path in apps/daemon". There is none — `grep -rn 'plan.approve' apps/daemon/src/` returns a single TEST FIXTURE hit. `plan.approve` is the CORE reducer's kind; the DAEMON's approval command is `approval.decide`. Confirm: daemon-command-registry.ts:45 maps it to CAPABILITIES.PLANNING, :94 pins its payload fields, and planning-services.ts:181 wires `"approval.decide": decideApproval`. Do NOT report blocked on the description's name.
2. Read `decideApproval` (planning-services.ts:146-179) end to end, including its comment: design 299 makes this one click and one transaction, and "returning early from any gate above it is what makes a partial approval unrepresentable". Note the three existing exits and their layers (DAEMON_INGRESS, DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, and `refuseFromCore` surfacing the core code unchanged), and that `activateInitialGraph` is the SINGLE durable commit.
3. Read `durableRun` (:123-133) — it reads the run via `stateOf(context.ledger, runId)`. That ledger record is the unit of work's durable identity and is where DoD 2's gate belongs.
4. VERIFY THE CONTRACT ON DISK: APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS, decideApprovalAuthority, grantHumanAuthority, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS all exported from the @moe/core ROOT. Note that checkHumanAuthority and refuseApprovalAuthority are deliberately NOT published — enter through decideApprovalAuthority only.
5. VERIFY THE DEPENDENCY EDGE by COMPILED PROBE with a negative control, probe deleted in the same command: import those five values plus types from the BARE `@moe/core` inside apps/daemon and typecheck. A root-barrel grep does not satisfy the rail.
6. FIND THE TIMER for DoD 5. `decideApproval` is synchronous and calls no setTimeout, so locate where `delayMs` actually LEAVES the daemon toward a timer. Record it; the bound goes there, not in a helper.
implementationPlan.note: Re-measured at HEAD ddb4753 without production edits. Confirmed daemon command is approval.decide: daemon-command-registry.ts maps it to PLANNING and pins its required payload; planning-services.ts wires PLANNING_HANDLERS['approval.decide'] to decideApproval. The handler's durable run read precedes applyApprovalCommand and activateInitialGraph is the sole durable commit, so the authority decision must early-return after durableRun and before the core approval reducer. Verified @moe/core root exports APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS, decideApprovalAuthority, grantHumanAuthority, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES/LAYERS and relevant types while deliberately withholding checkHumanAuthority/refuseApprovalAuthority. Dependency edge verified in apps/daemon/package.json (workspace:*), pnpm-lock apps/daemon importer (link:../../packages/core), and compiled bare-specifier probe: positive typecheck exit 0; negative missing-symbol control TS2305 exit 1; probe removed in the same try/finally command (PROBE_REMAINS=False). Repo search found no ApprovalAuthorityDecision.delayMs consumer or approval timer in daemon; decideApproval is synchronous, so the fail-closed bound must be applied when the authority decision leaves/is persisted by the daemon rather than passed to a timer.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD — WRITE THE DAEMON-LEVEL TESTS FIRST, in `apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-services.test.ts`.

DRIVE THE REAL HANDLER (DoD 1). Every case goes through `decideApproval` / PLANNING_HANDLERS with a real request and a real ledger context — never by calling `decideApprovalAuthority` directly. A test that calls the core function proves only what the core's own suite already proves, and repeats the "exports the symbols is not composition" failure that created this task.

CASE A — THE UNCONDITIONAL GATE. Sweep EVERY member of APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS against a GATED unit of work and assert the daemon refuses for each. Derive the case count from the imported array so a future member cannot slip past uncovered, but pin the member NAMES literally so the sweep cannot compare the array with itself.

CASE B — NOTHING ACTIVATED. For each refusal, assert that NO activation occurred — not merely that the call returned a refusal. A gate placed after `activateInitialGraph` would still return a refusal while the graph had already activated, and an assertion on the return value alone cannot tell the two apart. This is the test that pins ORDERING.

CASE C — CODE AND LAYER. Assert the stable code from APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES and the layer from APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS, literally. THREE layers can now refuse this handler (DAEMON_INGRESS, DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, and the authority's own), so each test states which answered. A gated case must be otherwise VALID — correct payload, matching exactRevisionHash — or an earlier guard answers first and the test proves nothing about the gate.

CASE D — UNGATED WORK IS UNCHANGED (DoD 4): an ungated approval still approves and activates exactly as before.

These fail until steps 3-4 land.
implementationPlan.note: Added daemon-handler TDD coverage. The sweep pins APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS literally, drives real plan.propose + approval.decide with otherwise-valid payloads, asserts APPROVAL_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED at HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE, no decision/approval event, and goal remains DRAFT; explicit ungated zero-delay control preserves approval/activation. Verified RED with the named test: vitest exited 1 at expect(outcome.ok).toBe(false), received true, proving the missing daemon composition.

implementationPlan.description:
PERSIST THE GATE ON THE UNIT OF WORK'S DURABLE IDENTITY (DoD 2). Create `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-gate.ts` plus its `.js` bridge rather than growing planning-services.ts, which is already 183 lines against a 250 target.

The gate lives in the DURABLE RUN RECORD that `durableRun` reads via `stateOf(context.ledger, runId)` — the same record carrying `submissionHash` and `state.goalRef`. It must NOT be a lifecycle or status field.

WHY THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: on 2026-08-15 a bulk promotion moved every BLOCKED task to PLANNING and CLEARED each task's recorded blockedReason as a side effect. A gate stored beside a status would have been cleared the same way, silently, for every gated unit at once. approval-authority.ts's own module comment states this; read it before designing the shape.

Write the read and the write so a gate that is present cannot be removed by any status transition, and so an ABSENT gate is distinguishable from a gate that failed to load — an unreadable gate must fail closed (treated as gated), never as ungated. Epic rail 4: unverifiable evidence never gains authority, and "could not read the gate" is exactly that.

TEST IT AS AN ACTUAL TRANSITION: drive a real status change over the ledger and assert the gate survives. A unit test of a setter would pass while the real transition cleared it — which is the incident.
implementationPlan.note: Added durable workIdentity.humanAuthorityGate persistence in the real plan.propose commit via approval-gate.ts/.js. The named test drives the real four-command planning lifecycle fold to durable PLANNING and reads the gate back from RUN_ID; focused run: 2 passed, 18 skipped, exit 0. Read semantics distinguish ABSENT from UNREADABLE and synthesize an ungranted sentinel for the latter so it cannot fail open. Daemon typecheck has no owned-path errors; the only current errors are foreign untracked src/telemetry/provider-run-codec.test.ts imports (provider-run-codec.js missing).

implementationPlan.description:
COMPOSE THE CONTRACT INTO THE HANDLER (DoD 1), in `apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-services.ts`.

Call `decideApprovalAuthority` inside `decideApproval`, positioned:
- AFTER `durableRun` resolves the runId, because the gate is a property of the unit of work and the work must be identified first;
- BEFORE `applyApprovalCommand`, so no core verdict is computed for gated work;
- and therefore necessarily before `activateInitialGraph`, the single durable commit.
An early return is the established idiom here — the handler's own comment says returning early from any gate above the commit is what makes a partial approval unrepresentable. Join that stack; do not add a check after the commit.

ENTER THROUGH `decideApprovalAuthority` ONLY. `checkHumanAuthority` and `refuseApprovalAuthority` are deliberately unpublished because decideApprovalAuthority consults the gate FIRST by construction (core/index.ts:135-138). Calling the gate directly would rebuild that ordering in a second place where a later edit could reorder it.

SURFACE THE REFUSAL UNCHANGED. Carry the contract's own code and layer out through the existing `refuseFromCore`-style path — the handler already surfaces a core reason code unchanged and that is the pattern to reuse. Do NOT translate an authority refusal into BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID or BOOTSTRAP_REVISION_HASH_MISMATCH; that would erase the very distinction DoD 3 requires the tests to pin.

Ungated work must take exactly the path it takes today (DoD 4). Run the step-2 tests: A, B, C must pass and D must still pass. Re-measure the file with `grep -c ''`; if it nears 250, move helpers into approval-gate.ts.
implementationPlan.note: Composed decideApprovalAuthority after durableRun identifies RUN_ID and before applyApprovalCommand/activateInitialGraph. The durable gate reader feeds the core entry point only; authority code/layer are surfaced unchanged. Expanded daemon ServiceRefusedBy from the core's published APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS (necessary scope growth so the typed daemon outcome can carry the required layer). Added real-handler unreadable-gate and REQUIRE_HUMAN policy tests. Fresh planning-services file: 22/22 passed, exit 0. planning-services.ts is 212 lines; approval-gate.ts is 78.

implementationPlan.description:
BOUND delayMs BEFORE ANY TIMER (DoD 5), at the boundary step 1 located.

`ApprovalAuthorityDecision.delayMs` is a safe non-negative integer, which is WIDER than setTimeout accepts. Above 2**31-1 setTimeout CLAMPS TO 1ms — so a delay meaning "effectively never" silently becomes "immediately", which is the worst possible direction for an auto-approval delay and is invisible in any test that only uses small values.

Bound it in PRODUCTION at the point delayMs leaves the daemon toward a timer. If step 1 found no timer inside the daemon, bound it where the decision is emitted or persisted, and say so in the module comment so the next consumer inherits the bound rather than re-deriving it. Bounding it inside a test helper proves nothing about production.

Decide and document what a beyond-range delay MEANS — clamping to the maximum safe timer value and treating it as "no auto-approval" are different behaviours, and the choice must be explicit rather than implied by whatever Math.min happens to be written. Fail closed: when in doubt, longer delay or require-human, never sooner.

Test it with a value ABOVE 2**31-1 and assert the production behaviour, not the clamp. A test using only realistic delays passes against the unbounded code and is exactly why this defect survives review.
implementationPlan.note: Added the production approval-delay boundary before any approval/activation. Because this daemon path has no timer, zero is IMMEDIATE, representable positive delays remain DEFERRED, and values above 2**31-1 explicitly become REQUIRE_HUMAN rather than reaching setTimeout and clamping to 1ms; both non-immediate dispositions fail closed as APPROVAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED @ APPROVAL_POLICY. TDD named oversized and ordinary deferred tests both went red on received ok:true before implementation. Fresh full planning-services file: 24/24 passed, exit 0.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE DESCRIPTION NAMES THE WRONG COMMAND, and a worker following it literally would find nothing and report blocked. It says "compose decideApprovalAuthority in front of the existing plan.approve path in apps/daemon". There IS no plan.approve path in apps/daemon — `grep plan.approve apps/daemon/src/` returns ONE hit and it is a test fixture. `plan.approve` is the CORE reducer's command kind (planning-run-reducer.ts:174); the DAEMON's approval command is **`approval.decide`**, and its handler is `decideApproval` at apps/daemon/src/planning/planning-services.ts:146, wired at :181 in PLANNING_HANDLERS. That is the composition point. I nearly filed a wrong block on the first grep; the correction came from reading the command registry rather than trusting the name.

WHERE THE GATE GOES, and the file tells you. `decideApproval`'s own comment says design 299 makes this ONE click and ONE transaction: "the plan/graph decision and the initial-graph activation commit together or not at all... returning early from any gate above it is what makes a partial approval unrepresentable." So the established idiom is an early return ABOVE `activateInitialGraph` — the single durable commit — and the authority check must join that stack of gates rather than being bolted in after the commit. Place it once the unit of work is known (after `durableRun` resolves the runId) and before `applyApprovalCommand`, so no core verdict is even computed for gated work.

SURFACE THE CONTRACT'S CODE, DO NOT RESTAMP IT. The handler already refuses with BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID @ DAEMON_INGRESS and BOOTSTRAP_REVISION_HASH_MISMATCH @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, and it has a dedicated `refuseFromCore` for surfacing a core reason code UNCHANGED — its comment says "whose reason code is surfaced unchanged". DoD 3 wants APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES / APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS asserted, so reuse that established pattern rather than translating the authority refusal into a BOOTSTRAP_* code. Translating would destroy exactly the distinction DoD 3 asks the tests to pin.

ENTER THROUGH `decideApprovalAuthority` ONLY. The contract deliberately does NOT publish `checkHumanAuthority` or `refuseApprovalAuthority` — core/index.ts:135-138 says so and explains why: decideApprovalAuthority "consults it FIRST by construction". Reaching around it to call the gate directly would rebuild the ordering the contract guarantees, in a second place, where a later edit could reorder it.

REJECTED: adding a plan.approve route to the daemon. That would be inventing an approval transport, not composing a contract, and the daemon's approval journey is deliberately `approval.decide` — recovery-completion.ts:129 even records that this handler is NOT reused elsewhere because it binds activation.

planningNotes.risks:
THE COMMAND NAME IS THE FIRST TRAP. The description says plan.approve; the daemon's command is approval.decide. A worker who greps the description's name finds a single test fixture and may conclude the path is absent and report blocked — which would be wrong and would strand a task whose prerequisite has already landed.

DoD 1 SAYS "THE REAL DAEMON HANDLER RATHER THAN THE CORE FUNCTION", and that phrasing is doing real work. A test that calls `decideApprovalAuthority` directly and asserts it refuses proves only that the core contract works — which its own suite already proves. The daemon test must go through `decideApproval`/PLANNING_HANDLERS with a real request, or this task repeats the exact "exports the symbols is not composition" failure that created it.

THE POLICY SWEEP MUST COVER EVERY MEMBER AND PIN ITS CARDINALITY. APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS is frozen at two today. Derive the case count from the imported array but pin the member NAMES literally; an expectation derived from the array under test compares it with itself and would survive a member being added later without daemon coverage.

PERSISTENCE IS THE INCIDENT'S ACTUAL MECHANISM. DoD 2 wants the gate on the unit of work's durable identity and a test proving a BULK STATUS TRANSITION does not clear it. The tempting shape — a field alongside lifecycle/status — is exactly what got cleared on 2026-08-15 when every BLOCKED task was promoted and each blockedReason vanished. Put it in the durable run record `durableRun` reads, and write the test as an actual status transition over the ledger, not as a unit test of a setter.

DO NOT RESTAMP THE AUTHORITY REFUSAL into BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID or BOOTSTRAP_REVISION_HASH_MISMATCH. Three layers can now refuse this handler (DAEMON_INGRESS, DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, and the contract's own), so every test must assert WHICH answered. `refuseFromCore` is the established surface-unchanged pattern — reuse it.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING AND UNTESTABLE BY SHAPE. The gate must be consulted before `applyApprovalCommand` and certainly before `activateInitialGraph`, which is the single durable commit for both halves of J1. A gate placed after the commit would still return a refusal while the graph had already activated — and a test asserting only the returned refusal would pass. Assert that NO activation occurred, not merely that the call refused.

delayMs CLAMPS SILENTLY. ApprovalAuthorityDecision.delayMs is a safe non-negative integer, wider than setTimeout accepts: above 2**31-1 it clamps to 1ms, so "effectively never" becomes "immediately" — the worst possible direction for an auto-approval delay. There is no timer in decideApproval, so step 1 must find where delayMs leaves the daemon and bound it THERE; bounding it in a test helper proves nothing.

SIZE: planning-services.ts is 183 lines against a 250 target. The gate check plus the delay bound will push it up; if it approaches 250, put the gate persistence and the bound in their own module rather than growing the handler file.
